statement.p: If the equation A\xvec = \bvec is inconsistent, what can we say about the pivot positions of the augmented matrix \left[\begin{array}{r|r} A \amp \bvec \end{array}\right]?

solution.p: We know there must be a pivot position in the rightmost column of the augmented matrix.

answer.p: We know there must be a pivot position in the rightmost column of the augmented matrix.

statement.p:
Consider the matrix A
A = \left[ \begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ -2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp -3 \end{array}\right] . If \bvec=\threevec{2}{2}{5}, is the equation A\xvec = \bvec consistent? If so, find a solution.

solution.p:
We construct the augmented matrix
\left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 2 \\ -2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp -3 \amp 5 \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -1 \amp 3 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \end{array}\right]\text{,}
which shows that the system is consistent. The solution space is described parametrically as
\xvec=\threevec{2}{3}{0}+x_3\threevec{2}{1}{1} .

statement.p: If \bvec=\threevec{2}{2}{6}, is the equation A\xvec = \bvec consistent? If so, find a solution.

solution.p:
Now the augmented matrix is
\left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 2 \\ -2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp -3 \amp 6 \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \end{array}\right]
showing that the equation A\xvec=\bvec is inconsistent.

statement.p: Identify the pivot positions of A.

solution.p:
There are two pivot positions in A, as shown.
\left[\begin{array}{rrr} {\mathbf 1} \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ -2 \amp {\mathbf 2} \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp -3 \\ \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr} {\mathbf 1} \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ 0 \amp {\mathbf 1} \amp -1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array}\right]\text{.}

statement.p: For our two choices of the vector \bvec, one equation A\xvec = \bvec has a solution and the other does not. What feature of the pivot positions of the matrix A tells us to expect this?

solution.p: Since there is a row of A that does not have a pivot position, it is possible to augment A by a vector \bvec so that we obtain a pivot position in the rightmost column of the augmented matrix. In this case, we have an inconsistent system.

answer.p: There is a row of A without a pivot position.
